page: Amazon Web Services m8i.16xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyperthreading, utilizing the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The CPU is equipped with 480 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for integer and tile operations. The system includes 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench multi-core execution, software compilation with Clang, and image processing. Static web serving throughput is also in the top tier, reaching 107.39 GB/sec. Single-core performance, measured via stress-ng, sits in the average tier, showing a clear performance tradeoff favoring multi-threaded workloads. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show strong read performance for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks, though large block write bandwidth remains in the average tier at 80.7 GB/sec.

For specialized workloads, the integrated Advanced Matrix Extensions enable strong performance in LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing where it reaches top-tier speeds on medium and large models. However, text generation for large models drops to an average tier due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. Given its balanced resource density of 4 GB RAM per vCPU and high-speed DDR5 memory, the m8i.16xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded enterprise applications, software compilation pipelines, database operations, and static web serving, provided that external storage is provisioned to offset the lack of local disks.
